Trusted by over 700 organizations worldwide, including 9 of top 10 US banks, Camunda helps enterprises boost operational efficiency, accelerate time-to-value, and deliver better customer experiences.

Fully remote and global, we are in the middle of something bigger: transforming into an AI-first organisation, built on our own platform. We use Agentic AI to automate, orchestrate intelligent processes, and elevate human contribution across every team.

About the role:

At Camunda, our Technical Account Managers (TAMs) are trusted technical advisors, partnering closely with our most strategic customers to help them turn their process orchestration vision into measurable business value. In this highly impactful role, you’ll be “in the boat together” with clients from day one – navigating technical challenges, providing expert guidance, and ensuring smooth adoption of our platform at scale. Success means building lasting relationships, accelerating customer outcomes, and making complex technology feel approachable for diverse teams. If you thrive on collaboration, love solving unique challenges, and are excited to empower companies across industries, we want you on our fast-growing, innovative Customer Success team.

What You Will Do

  • Guide the creation and execution of tailored technical adoption plans, designed to maximize business outcomes and ensure long-term success

  • Deliver hands-on technical guidance, best practices, and advisory services to both business and technical stakeholders – from onboarding through ongoing operations

  • Identify and remove execution risks by proactively conducting platform and solution health checks, facilitating escalation management, and advocating for customer needs internally

  • Foster strong, collaborative relationships with cross-functional Camunda teams such as Customer Success Managers, Consulting, Support, Product, Engineering, Sales and Pre-Sales to drive measurable customer outcomes at scale

  • Regularly spend time on-site with accounts for key milestone interactions (as needed, up to 50% during busy periods) to deepen partnerships and accelerate strategic initiatives

What You Will Bring to the Role

  • At least 3 years of experience as a Technical Account Manager or a directly comparable role in enterprise software

  • Demonstrated technical expertise: hands-on with a high-level programming language (such as Java, C#, or Python) and relevant enterprise software frameworks

  • Solid understanding of modern solution architectures and associated paradigms, including DevOps topics (especially Kubernetes)

  • A proven track record of building trusted relationships and providing advisory services to both technical and business stakeholders—able to synthesize and explain complex

  • issues clearly to varied audiences

  • Strategic problem solving competencies with a collaborative, impact-driven mindset; comfortable tailoring approaches to unique customer situations

  • Willingness and flexibility to spend time on-site with clients as account needs dictate (up to 50% during busy periods)


Nice to Haves:

  • Experience in enterprise automation, business process management, process orchestration, or robotic process automation

  • Relevant industry certifications (AWS Certified Solutions Architect, Azure Solutions Architect Expert, CKAD, CKA, etc.)

  • Familiarity with Camunda products

  • Ability and/or willingness to use our product.

  • Experience in enterprise automation, business process management, process orchestration, or robotic process automation

Equity: We also offer equity (where applicable) through our Virtual Stock Option Plan (VSOP).

Benefits & Perks

The Live Well program launches in 2026 and scales to €1,000 annually from 2027.

  • Financial Security: Retirement and pension plans (often with company contributions), plus life and disability insurance where relevant.

title: Technical Account Manager - UK
descriptionHtml:
The Role

Geordie is building the platform enterprises rely on to govern their AI agents safely — and we're growing fast. We're looking for a technical, customer-focused Technical Account Manager to own the post-sale relationship with our customers and make sure they get the best from their Geordie deployment, fast.

You'll be the technical face of Geordie for a portfolio of enterprise accounts — guiding onboarding and integration, becoming the go-to expert customers trust for anything technical, and working closely with our sales, product and engineering teams to keep our customers successful and growing. You will turn technical relationships into lasting partnerships.

This is a hands-on, technical role. You'll get deep into our platform, our customers' environments, and everything in between — and you'll help shape how Geordie delivers success for our customers as our first UK-based TAM hire.

We also expect you to work the way we build — intelligently and efficiently. That means embracing AI agents in your day-to-day workflows. We use tools like Claude Cowork to move faster and do more. If you're not passionate about that, this probably isn't the right place for you.

What You'll Do

  • Own the Technical Relationship — Be the primary technical point of contact for a portfolio of enterprise accounts, building trust from customer kick-off through renewal and expansion.

  • Project Management — Own the project plan for onboarding and major implementations end-to-end: timelines, milestones, resourcing, and risk tracking across customer, engineering, and product stakeholders. Run the cadence of standups/status calls, keep everyone accountable to dates, and escalate slippage before it becomes a surprise.

  • Onboarding & Implementation — Guide customers through deployment, integrations, and configuration, so they see value from day one.

  • Product Mastery — Become a deep expert on the Geordie platform. Troubleshoot issues, answer technical questions, and give customers confidence in how we work.

  • Adoption & Health — Track account health and usage, spot risks early, and drive the actions that keep customers engaged and expanding.

  • Escalation Management — Be the calm, capable owner of technical escalations — coordinating with engineering and product teams to resolve issues and close the loop with customers.

  • Renewals & Expansion — Partner with our sales team to identify expansion opportunities and ensure strong technical health underpins every renewal opportunity.

  • Customer Advocacy — Bring field insights back to our teams — feature requests, friction points, and what's actually happening in customer environments — so we keep building the right things and ensure the customer remains at the centre of everything we do.

  • Documentation & Enablement — Build the runbooks, guides, and best-practice materials that make onboarding repeatable and support scalable.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration — Work closely with sales, engineering and product teams to deliver a seamless customer experience.

  • Build the Function — As our first UK TAM, help shape the processes and playbooks that define how Geordie supports customers as we scale, in step with the wider TAM function.

What We're Looking For

  • You're technical, and you like it. You're comfortable in the details — agents, APIs, integrations, security, governance — and you enjoy figuring out how things really work.

  • You own outcomes. You don't wait — you track account health and get ahead of risk before it becomes a churn conversation.

  • You're a builder. Early-stage means you create structure where there isn't any and find a way to provide value to customers.

  • You're AI-fluent, not just AI-aware. You use tools like Claude Cowork and other agentic AI to run your own workflow — drafting runbooks, triaging tickets, prepping QBRs, chasing account health signals — so you spend your time on judgement calls and relationships, not repetitive admin. You look for the next task to hand off to an agent before you look for the next hire.

  • You earn trust at every level. You can debug an integration issue with an engineer in the morning and brief a CISO on progress in the afternoon, without losing credibility in either room.

  • You listen before you troubleshoot. You ask sharp questions to understand what's actually going on before you propose a fix, then deliver.

  • You communicate clearly and often. Customers always know where things stand.

  • You're focused on success. Not just at renewal time — all the time. You care whether customers succeed, and it shows in how you show up.

  • You embrace new ways of working. You actively use AI tools — especially agents — to work smarter, move faster, and do more. You thrive in ambiguity.

Requirements

  • 2–5 years' experience in a Technical Account Manager, Solutions Engineer, Sales Engineer, or Customer Success Engineer role at a SaaS or cybersecurity company.

  • Passion and interest in agents, how organisations are utilising them, their security and risk, and their governance.

  • Solid technical fluency — comfortable with agent architectures, agent security, agent tooling, APIs, SaaS/cloud integrations, and cloud environments.

  • Proven track record of owning post-sale relationships with enterprise customers, including onboarding, adoption, and renewal.

  • Experience diagnosing and resolving technical issues, including coordinating with engineering teams on fixes.

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work confidently with both technical practitioners and executive stakeholders.

  • Strong discovery and problem-solving skills — able to get to the root of a customer issue quickly.

  • Comfortable delivering polished, tailored product walkthroughs and training sessions independently.

  • Highly organised, with rigorous attention to detail across documentation, account health tracking, and follow-through.

  • Collaborative team player who thrives in a fast-paced, ambiguous startup environment.

  • Based in the United Kingdom, with the right to work in the UK, and the flexibility to travel to customer sites as needed.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience supporting security, AI/ML, or agentic tooling customers.

  • Active experience creating, deploying and managing agents.

  • Prior experience at a high-growth Series A–B SaaS company.

  • Light scripting or coding ability (e.g. Python) and comfort working with API tools such as Postman.

  • Relevant cloud or security certifications (AWS, Azure, or equivalent).

Why This Role

AI agents are changing how enterprises operate — and the question of how to govern them safely is becoming mission-critical. Geordie is the platform companies are turning to for that answer. As one of our first Technical Account Managers, you won't just be running a playbook — you'll be writing it. You'll have real influence over how we onboard, support, and grow our customers, and a direct line to Product on what to build next. If you want to go deep on a hard technical problem and build something that matters, this is it.

Our Values

Solve What Matters

We listen intently and stay focused on what truly matters to our customers. If it doesn't help them navigate real-world agentic adoption and risk, it's probably not worth building.

Build, Learn, Iterate

We favour momentum over perfection — testing, learning, and evolving through action. It's how we move fast and get better, together.

Kind, Not Comfortable

We're honest, respectful, and unafraid to challenge each other. We believe doing great work should feel good, too. Kindness makes that possible.

sA Platform for Your Best Work

We want this to be the most meaningful chapter of your career. Geordie is the place where you grow, lead and lift others, while building something that truly matters.

title: Technical Instructional Designer (AI Programmes)
descriptionHtml:
Multiverse is the upskilling platform for AI and Tech adoption.

We have partnered with 1,500+ companies to deliver a new kind of learning that's transforming today’s workforce.

Our upskilling apprenticeships are designed for people of any age and career stage to build critical AI, data, and tech skills. Our learners have driven $2bn+ ROI for their employers, using the skills they’ve learned to improve productivity and measurable performance.

In April 2026, we announced $70 million in strategic funding, led by Schroders Capital, with participation from StepStone Group, Lightspeed Venture Partners and General Catalyst. At an increased valuation of $2.1bn, the round makes us Europe’s first EdTech double unicorn.

But we aren’t stopping there. With a strong operational footprint and 800+ employees, we have ambitious plans to continue scaling. We’re building a world where tech skills unlock people’s potential and output.

Join Multiverse and power our mission to equip the workforce to win in the AI era.

The opportunity

AI can draft a lesson in seconds. It can't tell you whether that lesson will actually land with a nervous career-switcher three weeks into a Data or AI apprenticeship — or whether the concept it just explained is subtly, but fundamentally, flawed.

That's where you come in.

You'll be the human judgement layer sitting on top of our AI-assisted content pipeline — part subject-matter expert, part instructional designer. You'll decide what AI got right, fix what it didn't, and build the parts no AI can: the high-touch, high-stakes, deeply human moments in a learner's journey that make the difference between content that's technically correct and content that actually changes someone's career.

You'll have experience building content in generative and agentic AI, Data Analytics, and Data Science — not just someone who's read about it, but someone who can explain it, question it, and know when the AI-generated explanation of a neural network is actually going to help a learner or quietly confuse them.

What you'll actually do

  • Design outcomes, not just content. Apply end-to-end backward design to build Data and AI programmes where success is measured by what learners can do on the job — not just what they can pass a test on. You'll own the hardest part: turning a job-aligned outcome into a curriculum that actually gets learners there.

  • Chase real-world impact, relentlessly. When a piece of learning isn't landing — when a Data Analyst cohort isn't showing the outcomes it should — you won't wait to be told. You'll spot it, own it, and scope the revisions that bring it up to the standard it needs to hit.

  • Build what AI can't. Design the custom, high-touch programmes and creative assets — branching narratives, bespoke multimedia, high-stakes onboarding moments — that need real human empathy, creativity, and nuance. If AI could've built it, it's not your job; if only a person could, it is.

  • Put AI to work, deliberately. Use AI tools and prompt engineering to accelerate your own content development and uncover learning design approaches nobody's tried yet. This isn't about using AI because it's there — it's about knowing exactly where it earns its place.

  • Advise up, not just build. Work directly with Programme Designers and senior stakeholders on the quality and pedagogical effectiveness of AI and human output. Your feedback doesn't stay in the room — it shapes how our AI rules and frameworks evolve.

  • Prototype for the long game. Lead new learning formats and modalities that don't exist yet — and know how to balance shipping fast against building something sustainable enough to reuse.

What you'll bring

  • Real command of end-to-end ADDIE and backward design — you've built measurable, job-aligned outcomes and the assessments that prove learners hit them, not just theoretical frameworks on a CV.

  • A habit of treating "good enough" as a starting point, not a finish line — you notice when learning isn't driving real outcomes, and you take the initiative to fix it.

  • Genuine fluency with AI-powered tools and prompt engineering, used to accelerate content development and find genuinely new applications in Data/AI learning design.

  • The ability to take a genuinely complex AI, Data Science, or Analytics concept and design a learning experience around it that actually works — for someone with zero technical background.

  • The confidence and track record to influence peers and senior stakeholders toward a specific, measurable curriculum improvement — not just raise a concern and move on.

  • Resilience when things don't go to plan — you can point to a time a project hit a real obstacle (a blocker, a shifting SME, a launch that missed the mark) and describe exactly what you did about it, and what you learned.

What gets you in the door

You'll need at least one of these:

  • Hands-on experience producing technical content for Data Science or generative/agentic AI.

  • 2+ years designing instructional content in a commercial environment or for commercial clients.

  • Plus one of:

    • A Data Science degree (or close cousin of one)

    • Completion of a technical apprenticeship in Data or AI

    • 2+ years working as a practitioner in Data or AI

If you're a strong technical practitioner who's never formally studied instructional design, or a seasoned learning designer who's spent the last year deep in AI tools — either path can get you here. We're looking for the judgment, not a checklist.

What we'll actually explore together

We're upfront about what our process looks for, because we'd rather you come prepared to talk about the real thing than guess what we want to hear. Across the conversations, we'll dig into:

  • Advanced curriculum & applied design — how you turn an end-to-end backward-design process into measurable, job-aligned outcomes, and how you build creative assets that genuinely need a human touch.

  • Impact & excellence — what you do when a piece of learning isn't hitting its real-world mark, and how you weigh speed against building something built to last.

  • AI integration & innovation — where and how you've put AI tools and prompt engineering to work, and what that's actually unlocked.

  • Influence & stakeholder management — how you've moved a curriculum forward through a genuine disagreement or feedback conversation, not just delivered a good pitch.

  • Coachability & resilience — how you've handled a launch that didn't land, or a project blocker outside your control, and what you changed as a result.

 

Benefits

  • Time off - 27 days holiday, plus 5 additional days off: 1 life event day, 2 volunteer days, 2 company-wide wellbeing days (M-Powered Weekend) and 8 bank holidays per year

  • Health & Wellness- private medical Insurance with Bupa, a medical cashback scheme, life insurance, gym membership & wellness resources through Wellhub and access to Spill - all in one mental health support

  • Hybrid work offering - for most roles we collaborate in the office three days per week with the exception of Coaches and Instructors who collaborate in the office once a month

  • Work-from-anywhere scheme - you'll have the opportunity to work from anywhere, up to 10 days per year

  • Space to connect: Beyond the desk, we make time for weekly catch-ups, seasonal celebrations, and have a kitchen that’s always stocked!


Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

We’re an equal opportunities employer. And proud of it. Every applicant and employee is afforded the same opportunities regardless of race, colour, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression, or veteran status. This will never change. Read our Equality, Diversity & Inclusion policy here.

Our Commitment to Safeguarding

Multiverse is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of our learners. We expect all employees to share this commitment and adhere to our Safeguarding Policy, our Prevent Policy and all other Multiverse company policies. Successful applicants will be required to undertake at least a Basic check via the Disclosure Barring Service (DBS).

For roles that will involve a Regulated Activity, successful applicants must also undergo an Enhanced DBS check, including a Children’s Barred List check and a Prohibition Order check. Roles involving Regulated Activity may interact with vulnerable groups, therefore are exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 meaning applicants are required to declare any convictions, cautions, reprimands, and final warnings.

Providing false information is an offence and could result in the application being rejected or summary dismissal if the applicant has been selected, and possible referral to the police and the DBS.

title: Technical Product Owner
descriptionHtml:
Odaseva provides enterprise data management and security solutions that help organizations exercise sovereignty over their critical data. Companies representing 10% of global market capitalization trust Odaseva, including Schneider Electric, Volkswagen and Robert Half. Its Excalibur Data Platform enables customers to protect, secure, move, and use data and code independently of application vendors. The platform supports complex and high-volume use cases, including backup, archiving, zero-copy, BCDR & High Availability, data federation, and semantic AI orchestration. Customer-controlled end-to-end encryption raises the bar for enterprise security. With 11 patents, Odaseva manages 50 trillion records and supports 100 million users.

About the Role:

As a Technical Product Owner, you will be the driving force behind the delivery and lifecycle of our product features. Working within an Agile engineering team and partnering closely with our Tech Lead/Architect, you will act as the essential link between our customer-facing Product Managers and the development team.

While the Tech Lead drives architectural decisions and manages the engineers, you will take full ownership of the team's backlog, feature planning, and post-deployment success.

Because our current technical leadership leans heavily into complex systems architecture, we are looking for a proactive, communicative leader to champion Agile processes and cross-team relationships.

This role is perfect for a product-minded technical expert who enjoys being hands-on—regularly contributing to code and prototypes—while ensuring seamless delivery and alignment across the organization.

title: Technical Project Manager (m/w/d)

title: Technicien / Ingénieur Intégration & Validation Cryogénique
descriptionHtml:
Quandela est un leader mondial de l’informatique quantique, qui conçoit, développe et déploie des solutions quantiques de pointe à destination de la recherche et de l’industrie.

Son offre comprend notamment les ordinateurs quantiques les plus économes en énergie pour les data centers, des solutions complètes de calcul quantique accessibles via le cloud, ainsi que des services d’accès à des algorithmes pour les acteurs académiques et industriels.

Avec une feuille de route pragmatique et progressive, Quandela déploie depuis 2023 des systèmes de niveau industriel, tout en développant les futures générations d’ordinateurs quantiques tolérants aux pannes, capables de passer à l’échelle grâce à l’intégration de milliers de composants photoniques.

Quandela ambitionne de rendre l’informatique quantique accessible au plus grand nombre afin de contribuer à résoudre les défis industriels et sociétaux les plus complexes.

En savoir plus : Quandela | Leading Photonic Quantum Computing Solutions

Rejoignez-nous à la pointe de l’innovation en informatique quantique 🚀

À propos du poste

Dans le cadre du développement de nos activités de production et d'intégration de processeurs quantiques photoniques (QPU), nous recherchons un(e) Technicien(ne) / Ingénieur(e) Intégration & Validation Cryogénique pour rejoindre notre équipe Assemblage & Production, basée à Massy.

Vous interviendrez principalement sur l'intégration et la validation des équipements et sous-ensembles au sein des cryostats utilisés dans nos systèmes. Ces opérations impliquent la manipulation de composants sensibles et délicats, nécessitant une grande précision, de la méticulosité et une attention particulière aux conditions de montage et d'intégration.

Vous réaliserez les opérations de montage, de câblage, de thermalisation, de mise en service et de contrôle, en veillant au respect des contraintes cryogéniques et des protocoles de validation.

Vous participerez également au suivi du fonctionnement et des maintenances des équipements cryogéniques, notamment les cryostats et leurs compresseurs associés. La compréhension et l'utilisation des systèmes de vide et de pompage feront partie de vos activités, en tant qu'éléments nécessaires au bon fonctionnement des installations cryogéniques.

Au-delà de l'application des procédures, vous devrez être capable de comprendre le comportement des systèmes, d'analyser les anomalies et de contribuer à l'identification des actions nécessaires à leur résolution, en collaboration avec les experts techniques concernés.

Selon les besoins, vous pourrez apporter un support technique à distance ou intervenir ponctuellement sur les systèmes installés chez nos clients, en France ou à l'international.

Le poste s'inscrit dans un environnement de production en petite série, avec des équipements complexes et multidisciplinaires. La montée en échelle de la production est déjà engagée, notamment à travers la structuration progressive de nos méthodes et processus d'industrialisation. Une première base documentaire est déjà en place, et vous contribuerez à son amélioration afin de rendre les opérations plus robustes, reproductibles et adaptées à l'augmentation des volumes de production.

Vous bénéficierez d'un accompagnement et de formations internes pour approfondir votre connaissance des équipements cryogéniques spécifiques à Quandela, avec la possibilité de devenir progressivement un interlocuteur technique de référence sur ces systèmes.

Missions principales

Intégration et validation des équipements dans les cryostats

Vous réalisez l'intégration de composants et sous-ensembles, parfois sensibles et délicats, au sein des cryostats. Ces opérations nécessitent une grande précision et le respect des exigences de propreté, de manipulation et d'assemblage.

À ce titre, vous :

  • Préparez les cryostats, les composants et les équipements nécessaires aux opérations d'intégration.
  • Manipulez et assemblez avec précision des composants sensibles, en appliquant les précautions et méthodes adaptées à leur fragilité et à leurs contraintes d'intégration.
  • Réalisez le montage et l'intégration des composants et sous-ensembles dans les chambres de cryostats.
  • Assurez le passage, le cheminement et la fixation des câbles et connexions à l'intérieur des enceintes cryogéniques, en veillant à préserver l'intégrité des composants et des connexions.
  • Réalisez les opérations de thermalisation des câbles et composants, en tenant compte des contraintes thermiques et mécaniques.
  • Veillez au respect des contraintes d'intégration : encombrement, interfaces mécaniques, compatibilité des matériaux, propreté et contraintes thermiques.
  • Appliquez les bonnes pratiques de manipulation, de protection et de contrôle des composants tout au long des opérations d'intégration.
  • Réalisez les opérations de contrôle et de validation de l'intégration selon les protocoles définis.
  • Analysez les résultats des contrôles, identifiez les éventuelles non-conformités et participez à leur résolution.
  • Rédigez les rapports de validation associés et assurez la traçabilité des opérations réalisées.
  • Identifiez les difficultés d'intégration et proposez des améliorations adaptées.

Requirements

Compétences techniques – Indispensables

  • Bonnes connaissances pratiques en cryogénie et compréhension des contraintes associées aux basses températures.
  • Connaissance des principes de transfert thermique, de thermalisation et des contraintes mécaniques liées aux environnements cryogéniques.
  • Capacité à réaliser des opérations de montage et d'intégration de composants dans des systèmes cryogéniques.
  • Expérience dans la manipulation et l'assemblage de composants sensibles ou délicats, nécessitant précision et précautions particulières.
  • Maîtrise des bonnes pratiques de manipulation, de propreté et de protection des composants lors des opérations d'intégration.
  • Compréhension du fonctionnement général des cryostats et de leurs équipements associés.
  • Connaissance des principes de mise sous vide et du fonctionnement des équipements de pompage nécessaires aux applications cryogéniques.
  • Capacité à réaliser des opérations de mise en service, de refroidissement et de validation selon des procédures établies.
  • Capacité à réaliser et valider des opérations d'intégration selon des protocoles définis, à analyser les résultats et à rédiger les rapports associés.
  • Capacité à interpréter des mesures de température et de pression pour analyser le fonctionnement d'un système.
  • Capacité à réaliser les premières investigations techniques, à analyser les symptômes observés et à contribuer à l'identification des causes d'un dysfonctionnement, en collaboration avec les experts lorsque nécessaire.
  • Capacité à suivre des procédures tout en sachant identifier les situations nécessitant une analyse complémentaire ou l'intervention d'un expert.
  • Capacité à assurer le suivi des échéances de maintenance et des interventions réalisées.
  • Capacité à lire, appliquer et rédiger des procédures techniques et des rapports d'essais.
  • Sensibilisation aux risques associés aux systèmes cryogéniques et aux équipements sous vide.

Qualités recherchées

  • Méticulosité et précision : capacité à réaliser des opérations d'assemblage délicates avec soin, patience et une attention constante aux détails.
  • Rigueur et respect des procédures : attention portée à la qualité des montages, à la propreté des équipements et à la protection des composants sensibles.
  • Autonomie et esprit d'initiative : capacité à prendre en charge les activités confiées, à identifier les difficultés et à solliciter les bons interlocuteurs lorsque nécessaire.
  • Esprit d'analyse et de résolution de problèmes : capacité à comprendre le comportement des systèmes, à analyser les anomalies et à mener des investigations méthodiques.
  • Pragmatisme et sens pratique : goût pour les manipulations techniques, l'intégration et la résolution concrète de problèmes.
  • Organisation et traçabilité : capacité à documenter les opérations, suivre les essais et maintenir des historiques techniques fiables.
  • Curiosité technique et volonté d'apprendre : intérêt pour le fonctionnement des équipements et l'acquisition progressive d'une expertise approfondie.
  • Esprit d'amélioration continue : capacité à contribuer à la structuration des processus et à l'amélioration des méthodes de travail.
  • Capacité à travailler en équipe avec des profils techniques variés et à solliciter les experts appropriés.
  • Pédagogie et communication : capacité à transmettre des connaissances et à accompagner d'autres intervenants.
  • Respect des règles de sécurité et conscience des risques associés aux systèmes cryogéniques et aux équipements de vide.

Benefits

Ce que nous offrons :

      • Un rôle à fort impact, avec de réelles responsabilités dès votre arrivée
      • Une équipe qui a envie de collaborer, de partager et de grandir avec vous
      • Un modèle de travail hybride : 3 jours par semaine sur site à Massy, 1 jour à Paris et 1 à 2 jours en télétravail
      • Une exposition quotidienne à l’ensemble de la stack quantique : des API haut niveau jusqu’au firmware bas niveau, et tout ce qui se trouve entre les deux

Processus de recrutement :

      • Entretien avec l’équipe Talent Acquisition (30 à 45 min)
      • Entretien avec le Hiring Manager (45 min)
      • Étude de cas : en direct ou à préparer chez vous puis à présenter
      • Rencontre avec les équipes
      • 2 prises de références
      • Offre

Ce processus est donné à titre indicatif et peut évoluer en fonction du poste.

Chez Quandela, nous sommes convaincus que la richesse de notre équipe repose sur la diversité des expériences, des perspectives et des parcours. Nous nous engageons à construire un environnement de travail respectueux, inclusif et accueillant. Toutes les candidatures sont les bienvenues.

title: Test Development Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecrafts for humanity.

Here at The Exploration Company, we are developing, producing, and operating Nyx, a modular and reusable space orbital vehicle that can eventually be refuelled in orbit, and which carries cargo – and potentially humans in the long run. We are also developing different types of propulsion systems to power our future vehicles and missions. As a talented Test Development Engineer, you will be part of the team that is responsible for the development of test facilities for our future propulsion systems.


Key Responsibilities / Tasks:

In your capacity as a Test Development Engineer, your role will be continuously evolving, but day to day your duties may include:

  • Synthesise test bench requirements from user and operator needs and plan required verification methods and tests.

  • Translate engine test objectives and stakeholder needs into facility-level functional and performance requirements.

  • Perform technical trade-offs to determine the best choice of hardware, software, equipment, component, location etc for various test facilities.

  • Perform risk assessment analyses for future tests and developing mitigation actions to ensure personnel and hardware safety.

  • Provide technical inputs to cost, schedule, procurement, commissioning, maintainability, and facility acceptance planning.

  • Prepare and maintain P&IDs of test facilities based on test bench requirements and selecting components.

  • Undertaking preliminary design of the ground support equipment with minimal oversight.

  • Undertake hazard assessments of the test facility design (FMEA and HAZOPs) to determine if any additional changes to the design are required.

  • Work with the current test bench team to coordinate end-to-end activities of the development of test facilities including design, reviews, manufacturing, installation, commissioning, test operations, ongoing upgrades and maintenance.

  • Work with procurement, AIT and design teams during the development of test facilities to find the right balance of technical solutions, cost and lead time.

  • Presenting findings to team members and participating in design reviews and project discussions.


What we would love to see from you:

  • Bachelor's, master's or PhD in aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related field (Master’s and above preferred).

  • 2–5 years of experience in propulsion, test facility development, experimental engineering, or a related field.

    • Practical experience in the design, development, commissioning, or operation of test facilities, preferably for rocket propulsion systems.

    • Experience in test facility design for cryogenic propulsion systems is highly desirable. Relevant experience with other cryogenic or high-pressure fluid systems will also be considered.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret technical data, challenge assumptions, and make evidence-based engineering recommendations.

  • Proven ability to work autonomously on assigned technical topics while contributing effectively to a multidisciplinary engineering team.

  • Excellent communication and leadership skills, with the ability to convey complex concepts to diverse audiences.

title: Video Producer & Editor
descriptionHtml:
UFORCE exists to make aggression unaffordable.

Founded in Ukraine and headquartered in London, UFORCE is a defence-technology company with operations across Europe, the United States and Asia.

UFORCE builds uncrewed vessels, ground robotics and aircraft, autonomy software, and the command-and-control layer that operates them together. Each platform is deployable on its own, and stronger as part of the system. Its product lines include the MAGURA family of uncrewed surface vessels, the NEMESIS family of strike platforms, the LIUT family of ground robotic platforms, and counter-UAS systems.

As the Video Producer & Editor, you will be the point between raw footage and published work. The output goes onto company channels, into the hands of sales and government relations, and in front of closed-door audiences—including material that cannot leave the building.

Video is the clearest evidence of what UFORCE does to those outside the military. The systems are real, they are in use, and footage of them shows our customers what no render or animation can. In a market full of future-tense capability claims, that is the differentiator, and this role is what converts it into content people actually see.

This is not an assembly role. You are expected to shape and direct content as well as cut it: to decide what is worth capturing, what the film is, and what to leave out. The register is real and observed rather than advertised. The standard is publishable as it leaves the timeline.

It is a mid-level role with unusual freedom. There is no post-production team and no producer. The work is daily, the subject matter is serious, and there is room for someone who wants to build their craft on material most editors never get near.

 

What you will do

  • Cut and finish film for company channels, social platforms, sales and government relations, and internal and closed-door audiences.

  • Shape content from the outset: propose ideas, write shot lists and capture briefs, and direct or shoot capture where needed.

  • Deliver distinct cuts for distinct audiences rather than reformatting one film for all of them.

  • Finish to a publishable standard—grade, sound, captioning, titling and versioning.

  • Own the footage library: cataloguing, archive structure, backup and version control.

  • Hold the UFORCE film language and keep output consistent, including work delivered by external film-makers.

  • Travel to facilities, ranges, events and deployments, sometimes at short notice, and film in industrial and field conditions.

  • Utilise approved AI tools to optimize your workflow, strictly adhering to data security guidelines and ensuring no sensitive material leaves secure networks.

  • Apply the company's security and export-control requirements to footage, and route material showing platforms, facilities and personnel for clearance before release.

 

Required Skills

  • Around three to six years of professional editing experience, with a showreel of published work rather than showpieces.

  • Command of pacing, structure and sound, and the ability to explain the decisions behind a cut—particularly what was removed.

  • Experience in a factual, documentary, news or event register, not branded content alone.

  • Evidence of consistent output at pace, self-managed: media handling, versioning and deadlines without a producer.

  • A piece taken from idea and shot list through to final cut.

  • Fluency in a professional NLE—Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve or Final Cut—with working knowledge of After Effects or equivalent for basic motion work.

  • Sound judgement with confidential, embargoed or otherwise restricted material.

  • A point of view on what good looks like, and the willingness to argue for it.

  • Right to work in the UK and eligibility to obtain UK Security Clearance (SC level).

 

Nice to Have

  • Camera operation to a publishable standard, including commercial drone operation (with CAA certification).

  • Motion graphics and titling beyond basics.

  • Stills photography.

  • Experience cutting technical or engineering subject matter.

  • Experience in defence, dual-use or uncrewed systems, whether in industry or in service.

The nature of combat has changed.

Tomorrow’s battlefield success depends on autonomy, speed, and adaptability.

And UFORCE is ready.

descriptionHtml:

title: Werkstudent Engineering (m/w/d)
descriptionHtml:
Deine Rolle

Steuerberatung arbeitet mit strukturierten Daten, wiederkehrenden Abläufen und klaren Regeln, und kaum etwas davon ist bisher mit moderner Software neu gebaut worden.

Vogel berät mehrere Tausend mittelständische Unternehmen und baut über den Systemen, die wir kaufen, eigene Software: eine Datenschicht über DATEV, Werkzeuge für unsere Berater und Agenten, die wiederkehrende Arbeit übernehmen. Vogel ist kein Start-up und kein Konzern: etablierte Mandanten und echte, geprüfte Daten, und gleichzeitig ein Setup, das jeden Tag nach vorne geht.

Du studierst im Master Informatik, Wirtschaftsinformatik, Mathematik, Physik oder ein verwandtes technisches Fach, etwa an der TUM. Neben dem Studium willst du an Software arbeiten, die jemand am nächsten Tag benutzt, statt an einem Teilstück, dessen Nutzer du nie siehst.

Du arbeitest breit über Daten, Backend, Oberflächen und Agenten, direkt mit Moritz Vogel und mit den ersten Engineers, die wir gerade einstellen. Du arbeitest zwei Tage pro Woche, in der vorlesungsfreien Zeit gern mehr, abgestimmt auf deinen Vorlesungsplan. Wer überzeugt, steigt nach dem Master als Founding Engineer ein.

Deine Verantwortung

Werkzeuge für unsere Berater

  • Du setzt dich mit Steuerberatern und Buchhaltern an echte Fälle, findest heraus, wo die Arbeit hakt, und baust daraus ein Werkzeug, das sie am nächsten Tag nutzen.

  • Du baust Oberflächen, Dashboards und interne Werkzeuge vom ersten Prototyp bis zu etwas, das ohne dich läuft.

  • Dein Maßstab: Ein Berater würde es vermissen, wenn es abgeschaltet wird.

Daten und Integration

  • Du baust die Datenstrecken mit, die jede Nacht Daten aus DATEV und unseren anderen Systemen in unsere eigene Datenschicht laden, von Anfang an mit Prüfungen.

  • Du legst Kennzahlen so an, dass jede Zahl in jedem Werkzeug und jedem Bericht dasselbe bedeutet.

  • Du hilfst, die Systeme jedes übernommenen Hauses anzubinden, ohne dass daraus jedes Mal ein eigenes Projekt wird.

Agenten und Automatisierung

  • Du baust Agenten für wiederkehrende Arbeit mit und ziehst dabei die Linie zwischen dem, was das Modell beurteilt, und dem, was fest gerechnet wird.

  • Du sorgst dafür, dass jedes Ergebnis nachvollziehbar ist: welche Version, welche Quelle, welche Entscheidung.

  • Du prüfst gegen abgeschlossene, geprüfte Fälle statt gegen Testdaten.

Deine Perspektiven

Was du nach 3 Monaten geliefert hast:

  • Ein erstes Werkzeug von dir wird von einem Team im Alltag genutzt.

  • Du kennst die Datenstrecken aus DATEV und arbeitest sicher in unserer Entwicklungsumgebung.

Was du nach 6 Monaten geliefert hast:

  • Du verantwortest einen eigenen Baustein von der Anforderung bis zum Betrieb.

  • Andere bauen auf deinem Code auf, und deine Pull Requests gehen ohne große Nacharbeit durch.

Was du nach 12 Monaten geliefert hast:

  • Du arbeitest wie ein Engineer im Team und nicht wie eine Aushilfe.

  • Der Einstieg nach dem Master ist konkret: als Founding Engineer oder mit verlängerter Werkstudentenzeit bis zum Abschluss.

Wohin sich die Stelle entwickelt:

Werkstudent bei Vogel ist der Weg in den Berufseinstieg als Founding Engineer. Danach wächst du in die Verantwortung für einen eigenen Produktbereich, in der fachlichen Expertenlaufbahn oder in der Führungslaufbahn. Der Beitrag entscheidet, nicht das Berufsjahr.

Das bringst du mit

Erfahrung & Track Record

  • Masterstudium in Informatik, Wirtschaftsinformatik, Mathematik, Physik oder einem verwandten technischen Fach, an der TUM oder einer vergleichbar starken Universität.

  • Du hast schon Software gebaut, die andere benutzt haben: im Studium, in einem Werkstudentenjob oder in einem eigenen Projekt.

  • Profile, die nicht in dieses Raster passen, aber nachweislich gebaut haben, sind ausdrücklich eingeladen. Konkret: Bachelorstudierende kurz vor dem Master mit eigenem Projekt, Studierende der Physik oder Mathematik mit Engineering-Spur, Gründer eines kleinen Produkts. Wir bewerten am Beitrag, nicht am Etikett.

Skills & Arbeitsweise

  • Du schreibst sauberen Code in mindestens einer Sprache, idealerweise Python oder TypeScript, und kennst SQL.

  • Du arbeitest mit KI als selbstverständlichem Werkzeug, um Code zu schreiben, zu prüfen und zu testen, und weißt, wo sie danebenliegt.

  • Du willst Breite: Daten, Backend, Oberfläche und Agenten, nicht eine einzelne Schicht.

  • Du arbeitest auf Deutsch, weil unsere Berater und Mandanten es tun, und du bist regelmäßig vor Ort im Büro.

Mindset & Persönlichkeit

  • Du bringst die Demut mit, von Praktikern zu lernen. Der Steuerberater mit 20 Jahren Erfahrung weiß Dinge über seinen Prozess, die in keinem Diagramm stehen.

  • Du verträgst die direkte Zusammenarbeit mit der Geschäftsführung: schnelle Iteration, hohe Eigenständigkeit und manchmal Aufgaben, die nicht im Lebenslauf glänzen.

  • Du hast den Anspruch, in allem, was du ablieferst, den höchsten Standard zu setzen, nicht weil jemand es kontrolliert, sondern weil Mittelmaß dich persönlich stört.

Was du bei uns nicht finden wirst

  • Keinen Werkstudentenjob, in dem du Tickets abarbeitest, deren Nutzer du nie siehst. Du sitzt mit den Beratern am Fall und baust für sie.

  • Kein Werkstudenten-Setup nach Stundenkontingent ohne Entwicklung. Du wirst über die Zeit messbar besser und trägst mehr.

  • Keine Software-Firma. Wir sind ein Beratungsunternehmen, das seine eigene Software baut. Die Nutzer sind unsere eigenen Teams.

  • Kein Greenfield in einem leeren Raum. DATEV läuft, Mandanten warten nicht. Was du baust, muss neben dem laufenden Betrieb funktionieren.

FAQ

1. Was ist Vogel – und wo arbeitet ihr?

Vogel ist eine der führenden Mittelstandsberatungen Deutschlands – seit 1959, inhabergeführt in zweiter Generation, mit eigenem Kapital – und baut daraus die führende Beratungsplattform für den Mittelstand. Wir arbeiten an drei Standorten: Aalen als gewachsenem Stammsitz, Bopfingen im Kerngeschäft und München als neuem Hub. An allen dreien suchen wir quer durch die Funktionen – von Steuerberatung über Beratung bis zu den Teams, die das Fundament darunter bauen.

2. Wie sind die Gehaltsbänder zu verstehen?

Bewusst breit – und an jeder Stelle ausgewiesen, bevor du dich bewirbst. Wir differenzieren nach Track Record und Marktwert, nicht nach Abschluss: knappe, stark gefragte Profile am oberen Ende, weniger knappe am unteren. Die ausgewiesene Spanne ist kein Verhandlungsspielraum, sondern eine Profil-Skala – zwei Menschen mit ähnlicher Erfahrung können bei uns unterschiedlich verdienen. Was das obere Ende bestimmt, ist der Reifegrad, nicht die Zahl der Berufsjahre und nicht das Verhandlungsgeschick.

3. Wie viel – und wie – wird bei Vogel gearbeitet?

Gemessen wird an dem, was du bewegst, nicht an Stunden. Ehrlich ist aber auch: Wer 9-to-5 sucht, ist bei uns nicht die erste Adresse. Wir suchen Menschen, die aus eigenem Antrieb intensiv arbeiten, weil die Aufgaben es wert sind. Wie du deine Zeit verteilst, ist weitgehend deine Sache. Was wir teilen: Wir arbeiten präsent zusammen und sehen uns im Normalfall täglich im Büro – Kultur, Sparring und die besten Ideen entstehen in der täglichen Nähe. Wir sind keine Remote-Company und haben keine großen Home-Office-Policies; einzelne Remote-Tage sind kein Problem.

4. Wie läuft die Bewerbung?

Schlank, schnell, transparent – und nach Profil gestaffelt. In der Regel sind es vier Schritte: eine schriftliche Aufgabe, in der du zu acht Fragen Position beziehst – KI ist ausdrücklich erlaubt, wir bitten nur um eine kurze Selbstauskunft dazu; ein Gespräch von einer halben Stunde; eine gemeinsame Arbeitssitzung an einem echten Problem aus unserem Alltag; und ein Termin vor Ort mit dem Team und gemeinsamem Essen. Wie viele Schritte es tatsächlich werden, hängt von der Rolle ab: Bei Praktikum und Werkstudium fällt der Vor-Ort-Termin weg, für Schülerjobs genügt ein Gespräch, bei Senior-Rollen kommt ein gemeinsamer Arbeitsnachmittag dazu. Vorab kannst du einen Zehn-Minuten-Call buchen, in dem nur du fragst. In der Regel hörst du nach jedem Schritt innerhalb von 48 Stunden von uns.

5. Wie funktioniert die variable Vergütung?

Quartalsweise an Leistung gekoppelt, qualitativ bewertet. Die Skala steigt mit dem Level: bis 20 % Associate, 27,5 % Manager, 35 % Senior Manager, 42,5 % Director, 50 % VP. Erwartungswert bei guter Leistung – du erfüllst die Anforderungen, setzt eigene Akzente, bestehst den Keeper Test – liegt bei rund 50 % des Maximums; der Maximalbonus ist nicht der Normalfall. Im Fokus steht eine ganzheitliche Beurteilung durch deine Führungskraft anhand von sechs Kriterien: Impact, Judgement, Communication, Execution, Growth und Values.

6. Wie entwickle ich mich – welche Karrierewege gibt es?

Zwei aktive Wege: die IC-Karriere (fachliche Tiefe, Expertenlaufbahn) über die Stufen Expert, Senior, Lead und Principal – und die Management-Karriere (Führung, Personalverantwortung) über Manager, Senior Manager, Director und VP. Beide werden gleich vergütet, und beide müssen nicht nach oben führen: Wer auf einer Stufe bleibt und dort weiter in die Tiefe geht, ist bei uns genauso richtig. Die Richtung wählst du nach dem Onboarding, meist in Jahr 1–3. title: Werkstudent - Technisches Projektmanagement
descriptionHtml:
In the following you'll find information about us and the specific role:

Ort: Büro in Berlin Kreuzberg
Umfang: 20 h/Woche, flexibel einteilbar
Vergütung: 17–20 €/h
Arbeitssprache: Deutsch
Start: ab sofort
Auch als Vollzeit Praktikum möglich!

Was wir lösen

Die Energiewende ist relevanter denn je: Solaranlagen, Wärmepumpen und Wallboxen werden in Deutschland so schnell gebaut wie noch nie. Aber es gibt eine Bremse, die kaum jemand kennt - Bürokratie.

Was heißt das konkret? Jede einzelne Anlage muss beim Netzbetreiber angemeldet werden, bevor sie laufen darf.
Klingt einfach? Ist es nicht: In Deutschland gibt es über 850 Netzbetreiber - jeder mit eigenen Formularen, eigenen Prozessen, eigener Auslegung der Regeln. Kein Standard.
Für Installationsbetriebe heißt das drei bis vier Stunden pro Anlage, in denen ein Handwerker Formulare ausfüllt statt zu bauen.

Wir lösen das mit Software. Unsere Plattform erzeugt die Unterlagen aus den Daten des Installateurs und reicht sie automatisiert beim richtigen Netzbetreiber ein.
Unter unseren Kunden sind die größten Player der Solar- und Wärmepumpenbranche in Europa.
Und weil dieses Problem den Installationsbetrieben so weh tut, konnten wir im letzten Jahr von null auf über 1 Mio. € Umsatz gewachsen - bootstrapped, profitabel und ohne Investorengeld.

Deine Rolle

Du arbeitest im operativen Kern unseres Produkts und trägst Ownership für einen ganzen Bereich.
Dort sorgst du dafür, dass alles sauber durchläuft: Du behandelst die Edge Cases, kommunizierst mit allen relevanten Stakeholdern und betreust den Prozess so, dass er nicht nur jede Woche besser wird, sondern dass wir jede Woche mehr Kunden bedienen können. Denn genau da stehen wir: Mehr Kunden wollen unser Produkt, als wir heute live nehmen können.

  • Prozessbetreuung: Dein Bereich läuft, weil du ihn steuerst - von der Anmeldung bis zur Bestätigung durch den Netzbetreiber, inklusive der technischen Abstimmung, wenn etwas nicht passt.

  • Expansion: Du hilfst dabei, den Rollout in neue Netzbetreibergebiete voranzutreiben - neue Regeln erschließen, im System abbilden, live bringen. Und damit neue Kunden.

  • Produkt: Wenn etwas hakt oder du einen Impuls hast, baust du mit unserem Engineering-Team direkt die Lösung. Du gestaltest das Produkt aktiv mit - und skalierst damit unser Operations-Geschäft.

Was du mitbringst

  • Du studierst Ingenieurwissenschaften: Elektrotechnik, Energietechnik, Maschinenbau, Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen oder Ähnliches

  • Du arbeitest dich schnell in unbekannte Themen ein

  • Du treibst gerne eigene Bereiche voran, statt auf Anweisungen zu warten

  • Ausgeprägtes Auge fürs Detail - du findest Fehler, die nicht auffallen

  • Du bist in Berlin und kannst 20 h/Woche im Büro sein

Von Netzanmeldungen musst du noch nie gehört haben. Das lernst du hier in zwei Wochen.

Warum Voltir

  • Mission: Netzanmeldung ist einer der größten Engpässe der deutschen Energiewende. Du bist dabei, ihn zu lösen.

  • Wir leben AI-First: Ganze Bereiche wie Finance oder Go-to-Market sind bei uns One-Person-Teams, weil eine Person mit den richtigen Tools, Working Mode und Automatisierung sie trägt. Du lernst hier, wie das geht und bekommst Werkzeug und Wissen an die Hand, um es dir selbst anzueignen. Im heutigen Arbeitsmarkt ist das unglaublich viel wert.

  • Ein Startup, das durch die Decke geht: Du erlebst direkt mit, wie ein Unternehmen richtig groß wird. Von Fehlern zu gemeinsamen Meilensteinen, du sammelst echte Startup-Erfahrung.

  • Domain-Wissen, das du sonst nirgendwo bekommst: Netzbetreiber-Prozesse, Marktstammdatenregister, VDE-Normen, die Arbeitsweise der größten Solar- und Wärmepumpen-Anbieter Europas - du siehst den Renewable-Energy-Markt von innen.

Was wir bieten

title: Working Student - Backend Development Product Creation & Assignment (m|w|d)
descriptionHtml:
Are you in your first year of your Master's degree and looking for a working student role where you can contribute to real production systems, learn from experienced engineers, and explore the intersection of backend development, data engineering and AI? Then this could be the right role for you.

About the Team

The Product Creation & Assignment team at idealo builds the systems behind the automated expansion of our product catalogue. Products are the comparable entities users see on our platform — pages where offers from different shops are grouped, enriched and made comparable. We build the systems that identify and create new products from various data sources, and assign incoming shop offers to the right existing or newly created products.

We work on a modern, cloud-native stack combining JVM-based backend services with data-intensive AWS workflows: Java, Kotlin, Spring Boot, Kafka, MongoDB and EKS, as well as Python-based pipelines using MWAA, Lambda, Step Functions, DynamoDB, Glue Spark and S3. We integrate ML models and GenAI components into our production systems and actively use AI tools such as Claude Code in our daily development workflow.

About your new role

As a working student, you will contribute to meaningful work alongside a senior engineering team. Depending on your background and interests, your work may include:

  • Supporting the development and improvement of backend services and data workflows for automated catalogue expansion.

  • Working on product data quality — helping improve matching logic, data completeness and pipeline reliability.

  • Exploring how ML models and GenAI components (such as LLM-based matchers) can be integrated into production systems.

  • Contributing to tooling, observability and automation that makes the team more effective.

  • Participating in code reviews, pairing sessions and team rituals — learning how a production-grade engineering team operates.


Skills & Requirements

  • Currently enrolled in a Master's programme in Computer Science, Data Science, Software Engineering or a related field — ideally in your first year.

  • Solid programming foundation, ideally in Java, Kotlin or Python.

  • Some experience with backend development, data pipelines or cloud services — through coursework, personal projects or a prior internship.

  • Curiosity about data-intensive systems, ML integration or AI-assisted development.

  • Good communication skills and comfortable working in English and German.

At idealo you can expect

title: Working Student - LLM Inference Performance
descriptionHtml:
About Tensordyne 

AI is transforming our world. It can perform cognitive functions that previously only humans could do, such as perceiving interactions across different modalities and environments - with the ability to quickly learn and then solve complex problems. Tensordyne is an AI system solution company that builds very high-performance, low-power generative AI inference systems. Our mission, through the creation of custom silicon, hardware and software, is to enable multimodal Generative AI inference acceleration at scale, with safe, sustainable, high-performance systems for our hyperscaler and neocloud data center customers. We are at the leading edge of advancing the latest research and product improvements for generative Al inference solutions that will make Al even more advantageous for compelling new generative AI applications.Tensordyne is a well funded, fast-paced startup company with headquarters in both Sunnyvale, CA, and Munich, Germany. We also have many talented team members working remotely across North America and Europe. We take care of our people and their families with comprehensive benefits, competitive compensation, flexible spending options, and recognition programs, because building category-defining technology starts with a healthy, supported team. Come join us as we shape the future of multimodal generative artificial intelligence!

About the Role

How fast should an LLM building block run on our hardware? How fast does it actually run, and what would make it faster?

As a Working Student, LLM Inference Performance, you'll help answer these questions by working directly with our hardware and software engineering teams.

You'll write and optimize low-level kernels, benchmark performance on real silicon, and develop profiling tools that help engineers understand and improve LLM inference performance.

You'll gain hands-on experience with our Rust programming stack and Python SDK, use AI coding agents as part of your development workflow, and collaborate closely with engineers working on compilers, runtimes, and kernel optimization.

This is an opportunity to apply your academic knowledge to real-world AI hardware challenges while taking ownership of meaningful technical projects.

What You'll Do

  • Understand our hardware: Learn how Tensordyne silicon processes data, manages memory, and synchronizes operations, and how key LLM components such as attention, MLP, and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) routing map onto the architecture..

  • Develop and optimize kernels: Implement, test, and tune low-level kernels to improve the performance of LLM inference workloads..

  • Analyze performance: Build analytical and roofline performance models, compare predictions against simulator and real-silicon measurements, and investigate performance bottlenecks..

  • Build benchmarking and profiling tools: Develop benchmark harnesses, profiling scripts, and trace visualizations that make performance easier to measure, understand, and improve..

  • Work with AI coding agents: Explore workflows where AI agents assist with kernel development, optimization, and benchmarking, and identify the tools and context they need to work effectively..

  • Collaborate across engineering teams: Work closely with compiler, runtime, and kernel engineers to translate performance insights into practical improvements..

Example project: Develop a benchmarking and profiling harness for an LLM building block, such as decode attention, at two abstraction levels. Compare measured performance against theoretical estimates and make the tooling accessible to AI coding agents.

What We're Looking For

  • Currently enrolled in a Master's degree program in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mathematics, or a related technical field..

  • Strong programming skills in Python and at least one of C, C++, or Rust..

  • Understanding of computer architecture, memory systems, bandwidth, and parallel computing through academic coursework or personal projects..

  • Interest in low-level programming, hardware performance, and optimization..

  • Practical experience using AI coding agents in development workflows, with the ability to evaluate and improve their output..

  • An experimental mindset, with the ability to form hypotheses, analyze measurements, and communicate technical findings clearly..

  • Curiosity, initiative, and enthusiasm for learning new technologies..

Nice to Have

Experience in one or more of the following areas would be a plus:

  • GPU or AI accelerator programming..

  • Embedded systems or bare-metal programming..

  • Performance profiling, benchmarking, or optimization..

  • LLM inference fundamentals and architectures..

Why Join Tensordyne?

  • Work on cutting-edge AI technology: Contribute to the development of next-generation AI inference hardware and software..

  • Gain hands-on experience: Apply your university knowledge to real silicon and challenging engineering problems..

  • Own meaningful projects: Build tools and solutions that directly support our engineering teams..

  • Learn from experienced engineers: Work alongside specialists in hardware architecture, compilers, runtimes, and performance optimization..

  • Explore AI-assisted development: Gain practical experience building with AI coding agents and shaping how they interact with advanced hardware systems..

  • Make a lasting impact: Help develop performance tools and workflows that will support both current and future generations of Tensordyne technology..

Tensordyne's culture was built on the following values

  • Put people first. We only succeed when our people succeed.
  • Ethics and integrity always. Be open, honest, and respectful of everyone.
  • Think Big. Be ambitious and have audacious goals.
  • Aim for excellence. Quality and excellence count in everything we do.
  • Own it and get it done. Results matter!
  • Make each person better together than they would be as an individual.
  • Embrace each other’s differences, and embrace that there will be differences.

Tensordyne is an equal opportunity employer. We believe diverse teams are better equipped to solve complex problems and build exceptional technology. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, color, gender identity or expression, marital status, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, race, religion, pregnancy, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances.
